symbols.name: X
symbols.def: Covariate under the population specified by context.

symbols.name: S
symbols.def: Population indicator; \(S=1\) is source and \(S=0\) is target.

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: Observed treatment receipt in the source sample.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: Observed outcome in the source sample.

symbols.name: P_S
symbols.def: Observed source law induced by \(P_n^F\) given \(S=1\) and source assignment.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: Joint law inducing the two observed samples.

symbols.name: C_n
symbols.def: Confidence set measurable with respect to its declared inputs.

symbols.name: \mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)
symbols.def: Members of \(\mathcal P_n\) whose source covariate law, transport weight, and propensity equal the geometry \(\mathfrak g\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak C^{\mathrm{or}}(\mathfrak g)
symbols.def: Oracle procedures honest uniformly over \(\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)\).

symbols.name: V_{\mathfrak g}^\star
symbols.def: The conditional minimax expected-length frontier defined in def:fixed-geometry-value.

symbols.name: c_-
symbols.def: Lower regularity constant for source-cell probabilities.

symbols.name: c_+
symbols.def: Upper regularity constant for source-cell probabilities.

symbols.name: \mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}
symbols.def: The regular nonuniform finite-cell class in def:regular-finite-cell-class.

symbols.name: \mathfrak C^{\mathrm{reg}}
symbols.type: class of regular-cell honest procedure sequences
symbols.def: Procedures using the two samples and known \((q_{x,n})\) and \(e\), but not \(w\), that are honest over \(\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\).

novel.justification: Bounded potential outcomes are routine for minimax expected-length analysis of binary or rescaled outcomes. This load-bearing restriction forces the causal ratio to have a finite range rather than importing an arbitrary truncation.

assumptions.condition: \((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n\sim P_S^{\otimes n}\), \((X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n}\sim P_T^{\otimes N_n}\), \((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n\perp(X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n}\), and \(N_n/n\to c\).
\(\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[Y^Z(1)-Y^Z(0)\mid X=x,S=0]=\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[Y^Z(1)-Y^Z(0)\mid X=x,S=1]\) for \(P_T\)-almost every \(x\).

standard.name: conditional transport of the assignment-outcome contrast

assumptions.condition: \(\mathbb E_{X\mid S=0}[\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[D(1)-D(0)\mid X,S=0]]=\mathbb E_{X\mid S=0}[\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[D(1)-D(0)\mid X,S=1]]\).

standard.name: integrated transport of the first stage

novel.justification: Calibrated or coarsened transport designs can impose an externally auditable density-ratio cap while allowing the cap to grow with increasingly distinct target populations.
The condition permits growing Kish design effects realized by finite calibration tables while retaining a transparent overlap scale.
A target recruitment shift can simultaneously concentrate covariates in poorly represented strata and reduce the target complier share.
Published calibration tables can fix source-cell shares and assignment probabilities while a registry leaves only the target cell probabilities unknown.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal P_n\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n=\{P=(P_n^F,e):P\text{ satisfies ass:full-data-support, ass:population-presence, ass:two-sample-array, ass:instrument-overlap, ass:source-observation, ass:iv-randomization, ass:iv-exclusion, ass:iv-monotonicity, ass:outcome-transport, ass:receipt-transport, ass:target-complier-positivity, ass:transport-domination, ass:weight-envelope, ass:weight-second-moment, and ass:degrading-array at index }n\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal N_n\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal N_n=\{P\in\mathcal P_n:P\text{ satisfies ass:finite-cell-source at index }n\}\).

definitions.name: transported-score inversion handle
definitions.construction: For every \(\vartheta\in\Theta\), form the source inverse-propensity score \(w(X)\{Z/e(X)-(1-Z)/(1-e(X))\}(Y-\vartheta D)\), compare its empirical mean with \(L_\alpha\{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nw(X_i)^2/n\}^{1/2}\), and invert the resulting acceptance inequality over \(\Theta\).  Once \(w\) and \(e\) are oracle-known, the target sample does not enter this score.

definitions.name: fixed-strength geometry handle
definitions.construction: Hold an arbitrary admissible deterministic array \((P_S^X,w,e)\) fixed, set \(\mu_n=(t_0\kappa_n/n)^{1/2}\) and the conditional complier probability \(p_n(x)=\mu_nw(x)/\kappa_n\), vary only the complier outcome mean over a continuum, and compare every member with its center by chi-square and total variation.

definitions.name: fixed-geometry continuum witness
definitions.construction: Fix \(\mathfrak g=(P_S^X,w,e)_{n\ge1}\in\mathcal G\) and \(t_0>0\).  Set \(\mu_n=(t_0\kappa_n/n)^{1/2}\), \(p_n(x)=\mu_nw(x)/\kappa_n\), \(\rho=(1-\alpha)/8\), and \(H(t_0)=\min\{1/4,\rho t_0^{-1/2}\}\).  Conditional on \(X=x\), assign compliance types \((D(0),D(1))=(0,1),(1,1),(0,0)\) probabilities \(p_n(x),(1-p_n(x))/2,(1-p_n(x))/2\).  Set \(Y(0)=0\); for compliers let \(Y(1)\) be Bernoulli \((1/2+h)\), and for both always-takers and never-takers let \(Y(1)\) be Bernoulli \((1/2)\), for \(|h|\le H(t_0)\).  Use this same conditional full-data law in both populations, draw source encouragement with propensity \(e(X)\), and denote the resulting joint observed-data law and fixed oracle inputs by \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal G\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G\) is the class of deterministic arrays \(\mathfrak g=(P_S^X,w,e)_{n\ge1}\) such that \(P_S^X\) is a probability law on \(\mathcal X\), \(e:\mathcal X\to[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), \(w:\mathcal X\to[0,2k_n]\), \(\mathbb E_S[w(X)]=1\), \(\kappa_n=\mathbb E_S[w(X)^2]\le k_n\), and \(P_T(A)=\mathbb E_S[w(X)\mathbf 1\{X\in A\}]\) for every measurable \(A\subseteq\mathcal X\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)\)
definitions.construction: For \(\mathfrak g\in\mathcal G\), \(\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)=\{P\in\mathcal P_n:(P_S^X,w,e)\text{ equals the index-}n\text{ component of }\mathfrak g\}\).

definitions.name: \(V_{\mathfrak g}^\star(t_0)\)
definitions.construction: \(V_{\mathfrak g}^\star(t_0)=\inf_{(C_n)\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{or}}(\mathfrak g)}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g):\,t_n\ge t_0}\mathbb E_P[\lambda(C_n)]\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{P\in\mathcal P_n:\mathcal X=\{1,\ldots,k_n\},\;q_{x,n}=P_S^X(X=x),\;c_-/k_n\le q_{x,n}\le c_+/k_n\text{ for every }x\}\), where \(0<c_-\le1\le c_+<\infty\) are fixed.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), source randomization identifies \(\Delta_Y(x)=\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[Y^Z(1)-Y^Z(0)\mid X=x,S=1]\) and \(\Delta_D(x)=\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[D(1)-D(0)\mid X=x,S=1]\). Outcome-contrast transport and integrated first-stage transport imply \(\mu_{Y,n}=\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[(Y(1)-Y(0))\mathbf 1\{D(1)>D(0)\}\mid S=0]\) and \(\mu_n=P_n^F(D(1)>D(0)\mid S=0)\). Hence \(\mu_{Y,n}/\mu_n=\theta_T=\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid D(1)>D(0),S=0]\in\Theta=[-1,1]\).
statements.justification: The proposition makes the target a genuine causal estimand and establishes that compactness follows from the full-data outcome bound.
statements.gap: Dufour (1997) addresses an unbounded locally unidentified coefficient, not an intrinsically bounded target complier effect.
statements.consumer: It supplies the finite-diameter premise for the frontier.

statements.statement: There exist constants \(c_0>0\) and \(t_c>0\), depending only on \(\alpha\), \(\varepsilon\), and the fixed class constants, such that for every \(t_0>0\), \(V^\star(t_0)\ge c_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}\) and \(V_{\mathcal N}^\star(t_0)\ge c_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}\). In particular, \(V^\star(t_0)\ge c_0\) whenever \(0<t_0\le t_c\). The constants do not depend on the decomposition of \(t_0\) into \(\mu_n\) and \(\kappa_n\).
statements.justification: The converse tests whether Kish deflation is an information bound rather than a variance diagnostic.
statements.gap: Mikusheva (2010) treats invariant linear-IV arc length, while Armstrong and Kolesar (2021) treat regular overlap-sensitive ATEs; neither supplies this transported causal-ratio converse.
statements.consumer: It identifies regimes where even an oracle cannot give a short honest set in deep-canvassing and transported-encouragement studies.

statements.statement: Does there exist one \((C_n)\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{or}}\), obtained by the transported-score inversion handle, and a constant \(C_0>0\) such that \(R((C_n),t_0)\le C_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}\) simultaneously for every \(t_0>0\)? In the same construction, is this order invariant up to universal constants across all nondegenerate admissible weight geometries sharing \(t_n\) under \(w\le2k_n\)?
statements.justification: A single sequence is needed for simultaneous all-strength validity, and the fixed-strength geometry clause determines whether the Kish index is sufficient rather than mnemonic.
statements.gap: Chen and Huang (2025) provide regular transported inference; Smucler, Lanni, and Masip (2025) provide single-population unbounded score inversion; Choi and Shen (2019) implement two-sample linear-IV robust sets. None resolves simultaneous compact transported-CACE expected-length attainment or fixed-​strength weight-geometry equivalence.
statements.consumer: It would give one confidence procedure for target-CACE analyses where compliance and covariate representativeness both deteriorate.

statements.statement: On \(\mathcal N_n\), does there exist one sequence \((C_n)\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{cell}}\) and a constant \(C_0>0\) such that \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n:\,t_n\ge t_0}\mathbb E_P[\lambda(C_n)]\le C_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}\) simultaneously for every \(t_0>0\)?
statements.justification: This isolates whether estimating the target cell distribution introduces an information bottleneck beyond the oracle frontier.
statements.gap: Rudolph and van der Laan (2017) and Zeng et al. (2024) learn transport nuisances under regular target effects, not under this weak-ratio growing-cell sequence.
statements.consumer: It determines whether a covariate-only target registry is sufficient for weak-identification-robust transported encouragement inference.

statements.statement: If \(w(X)=1\) \(P_S\)-almost surely, then \(\kappa_n=1\) and \(t_n=n\mu_n^2\); hence the frontier specializes to compact single-population weak-ratio inference.
statements.justification: When \(w=1\), the effective-strength index reduces to the familiar single-population weak-ratio index \(n\mu_n^2\).
statements.gap: The proposition is an index reduction; the fixed-geometry theorem supplies the separate two-sided minimax statement on the no-shift slice.
statements.consumer: It connects the transported frontier to compact single-population weak-ratio inference without conflating the two experiments.

sampling_model.units: Source units contribute \((X,Z,D(Z),Y(D(Z)))\); target units contribute only \(X\).
sampling_model.treatment: \(Z\) and \(D(z)\) are binary; \(Y(d)\in[0,1]\) in both populations.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The oracle frontier reveals \(w\) and \(e\); the finite-cell question withholds \(w\) and retains known uniform source cells and \(e=1/2\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Identifies target CACE as a transported Wald ratio and gives regular weighted and multiply robust asymptotics.
Develops efficient-influence-function and TMLE inference for transported encouragement effects with target assignment and receipt observed.
Constructs a high-dimensional orthogonal Anderson--Rubin LATE test with weak-identification-robust size in one population.
Establishes weak-IV-uniform score-set validity and unbounded set geometry for a one-population LATE.
Extends weak-instrument-robust Anderson--Rubin, Kleibergen, and conditional likelihood-ratio inference to linear two-sample IV regression.
Implements weak-instrument-robust confidence sets for a linear two-sample IV model with possibly heterogeneous samples.
Shows near-shortest expected arc length for CLR sets within an invariant linear weak-IV class.
Establishes unbounded-confidence-set impossibility under local nonidentification of an unbounded parameter.
Derives optimal honest inference for regular ATEs under limited overlap and smoothness restrictions.
Derives regular efficiency and minimax results for transported causal effects.

tldr: The transported complier effect is forced into \(\Theta=[-1,1]\), and its honest expected-length frontier is governed by the effective strength \(t_n=n\mu_n^2/\kappa_n\).  A universal fixed-geometry converse and one oracle source-score inversion sequence match at order \(\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}\) for every fixed threshold \(t_0\), uniformly over admissible weight and propensity geometries.  Unknown target cell probabilities cost no minimax order on \(\mathcal N_n\), and the feasible result extends to known regular nonuniform source-cell probabilities and known cell-varying propensities.

project_justification.gap: Existing weak-instrument work does not give a finite minimax expected-length frontier for a transported causal ratio under jointly vanishing target first stages and diverging transport-weight dispersion.
project_justification.niche: The note isolates the single effective-strength index \(t_n=n\mu_n^2/\kappa_n\), treats the oracle experiment geometry by geometry, and separately studies feasible target-weight learning in structured finite-cell designs.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves matching lower and upper oracle frontiers, including a converse conditional on every admissible fixed geometry, and proves that estimating target cell probabilities causes no order loss on the uniform finite-cell class or its known regular nonuniform extension.  Feasibility with an unknown assignment propensity and feasibility beyond finite cells remain outside the established scope.

related_work: Dufour (1997), Gleser and Hwang (1987), and Bertanha and Moreira study impossibility phenomena driven by unbounded parameter spaces; that premise fails here because bounded outcomes and binary treatment force \(\Theta=[-1,1]\).  Mikusheva studies weak linear-IV confidence-set geometry, while Ma and Smucler et al. study single-population weak-IV-robust LATE procedures with learned nuisances.  Aronow, Chang, and Lopatto study finite-population LATE without transport reweighting, and Ren studies strong-overlap within-population MTE extrapolation.  Chen and Huang provide the transported-LATE identifying functional, while Rudolph and van der Laan and Ross et al. motivate transported complier-effect applications.  In contrast to coverage-only or regular-asymptotic guarantees, this paper gives a matched oracle minimax expected-length frontier and a matched feasible frontier for structured finite-cell weight learning.
interpretation: The order-one elbow may be normalized at \(t_c=1\), but this is not a sharp critical constant.  Below an order-one effective-strength level the theorem proves a nonvanishing lower bound on worst-case expected length; it does not claim that every honest set converges to the full diameter two.  The same score-inversion sequence obeys the bound at each fixed \(t_0>0\); this is not a joint moderate-deviation assertion for moving thresholds \(t_{0,n}\).
technical_internal_limitation: The order result deliberately uses crude Chebyshev and collision-U-statistic constants and does not claim practical or sharp calibration.  The fixed-geometry converse is complete.  The remaining technical limitation is feasibility outside known regular finite-cell source designs: unknown propensities require control of random cell denominators and their scale estimate, while continuous-covariate sieves require approximation assumptions, weak-denominator bias control, and a partition-complexity rule.
honest_scope: Proved results are the transported identifying ratio, its forced compact range, the matched global and fixed-geometry oracle frontiers, one geometry-uniform oracle score-inversion sequence, and matched feasible target-cell weight learning on the uniform class \(\mathcal N_n\) and a known regular nonuniform-cell extension with known cell-varying propensity.  The oracle result is not presented as a feasible general-model procedure.  No claim is made for unknown assignment propensities, continuous-covariate weight learning, sieve approximation, moving strength thresholds, disconnected-set taxonomy, or sharp constants.
